problem: Closed monomorphization does not preserve an arbitrary generic public export. Direct declarations require a source generic API to have an actual callable export.
input: The same PsValidatedIrModule obtained by strict RuntimeIR validation; no weakening of generic scope, type or invariant checks.
selection: PsUniformSpecializedIrModule retains exactly the validated RuntimeIR, including unused generic declarations and all static type arguments. It is a distinct selection wrapper, not PsSpecializedIrModule or a live authority token.
target: Direct JS with the existing 64-bit scalar representations, JavaScript value parameters, arrays and object field/tag layouts. Type arguments affect static checking but do not become runtime arguments.
lowering: Shared policy-aware lowerer checks supported type forms and intrinsic arities, then drops static type annotations/arguments. Unknown types remain unsupported. Existing WithProfile APIs pass the closed policy and retain all prior rejection behavior.
stages: psCompilerUniformJavaScriptStagesFromPrepared emits uniformSpecializedIr instead of specializedIr. Shared prepared-input capture, strict validator, JsIR validator, encoder and stack-safe printer avoid parallel implementations.
correspondence: The bounded host checker verifies the explicit envelope and exact byte identity with caller-selected VerifiedIR. It does not infer strict validity from serialized bytes or prove target representation adequacy.
unsupported: Foreign/imported functions in this initial uniform profile
Dependent runtime values or new runtime representation primitives
Higher-rank/named public types and generic constant declarations without a runtime function
Automatic representation selection and production checked CLI routing
compatibility: Closed specialization, its ground-type requirements, Wasm/default-JS profiles and existing APIs remain unchanged. The new entry is selected explicitly; no fallback after closed specialization failure.
remaining: Higher-rank/named public types and generic constant policies
Expression and declaration-position maps, portable map serialization and automatic linking
Uniform source/target preservation argument and later independent assurance
hostSelection: createCheckedCompilerService selects javaScriptRepresentation once at construction; default is closed. A uniform session requires its exact selected staged API, checks every required stage and exact VerifiedIR/envelope identity, and cannot fall back to closed or legacy APIs. Logical source certificates remain separate from representation selection.
declarations: The explicitly paired psc-direct-js-declarations-uniform-structural/1 profile consumes exact source PublicApiIR and uniform selection subjects. It retains prefix source generics, checks alpha-correspondence with RuntimeIR, and binds complete JsIR export inventory without inferring signatures from instances. The same frozen prepared source feeds the portable interface-ts writer; the checked service requires exact agreement with independently checked host bytes before publication.
archive: The common graph records psc-pass-uniform-specialize/1 and psc-uniform-ir-to-js-ir/1 with exact profile parameters. Explicit context selection derives the JS registry; descriptors, target profiles, actions, queries and bundles bind it. Fresh archive replay checks the exact envelope relation, complete target inventory and all declaration subjects.
origins: Shared declaration composition reconstructs exact observed source/erasure/print metadata and pins the uniform artifact plus VerifiedIR. Edges identify actual retained RuntimeIR declarations, without synthetic specialization instances. Standalone ECMA-426 maps use recipe/2 and selected derivation/3; archived earlier derivations remain unchanged.
